title: [CQ-F12] Contract integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Verify revision/receipt behavior across daemon/proxy/launchers, restarts, reassignments and legacy-to-strict cutover.

Deliverable: Contract integration and hardening. This is task F12 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F08, F10, F11.
definitionOfDone: All held-out authorization races pass unchanged.
Execution-only progress does not invalidate receipts by revising approval.
Producer candidate provenance remains distinct from current QA attempt.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Completion readiness before finalizing (hardening; test first).

Phase 0, before any edit:
- Confirm CQ-F12a (task-b5f743bc50544d838422ce365616240e) and CQ-F12b (task-3ead73b368094850bfec955c316bc239) have landed: get_context epicSiblings[].landing.merged, or `git log moe/work-2026-10-24 --grep 'Moe-Task: <id>'`.
- Record the sha256 of the two held-out race files: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts and packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts. They are never edited (DoD1).

Test first. In completionAuthorization.test.ts, the DoD3 describe has the case 'passes complete_task on current evidence through to the readiness backstop'. Turn it into 'refuses complete_task at the readiness gate before any write, so a retry gets the same refusal':
- after finish(), call the file's own refused('task', {}, 'EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY') helper TWICE. The helper already asserts no updateTask, touchWorker, writeEntity or postToRoleChannel call, and identical bytes;
- then assert getAttempt(h.state, attempt.id)?.phase === 'running', and that the task is still WORKING with assignedWorkerId 'worker-s'.
- Confirm it is RED at HEAD. Today complete_task calls setAttemptPhase(...'finalizing') (a writeEntity) before taskStore.updateTask's progression backstop throws. So the first refused() fails on the write spy, and a retry would get ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING.

Fix in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeTask.ts:
- Import assertExecutionProfileReady and resolveTaskExecutionProfile from '../delivery/executionProfile.js'.
- Call assertExecutionProfileReady(resolveTaskExecutionProfile(state.project?.settings, task.executionPolicySnapshot)) directly after the `if (strict) assertCompletionEvidenceEligible(...)` line. That places it with the other read-only refusals, BEFORE checkBranchPolicy (which can post to #governors) and before currentAttempt/setAttemptPhase('finalizing').
- It evaluates exactly the expression that taskStore's private assertProgressionReady evaluates for complete_task's WORKING->REVIEW write. isNewProgression is true there because the caller update never sets assignedWorkerId:null. util/claimEligibility.ts uses the same idiom.
- Legacy/observe behaviour is unchanged: the call is a no-op, and a malformed setting or snapshot has already failed closed inside assertExecutionAuthorized.
- Leave the store backstop in place (defense in depth).
- Add a one-line comment on why it runs before finalizing.
- Error handling: the refusal is thrown before any write, so there is nothing to roll back.
- Known precedence change, acceptable and to be documented in step 6: on a verified-local row, NOT_READY now precedes BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL.

Run only this file, in the isolated Linux snapshot (Serena memory gotcha-linux-vitest-reuse-native-node-modules; every MOE_* unset): `npx vitest run src/tools/completionAuthorization.test.ts`.

E2E harness and DoD2: one served-context receipt carries execution-only progress across a daemon restart and the legacy-to-strict cutover.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/__e2e__/executionContract.e2e.test.ts. npm test picks it up, like lifecycle.e2e.test.ts, which shows the real-tool flow to mirror.
- Drive REAL tool handlers through ToolTestHarness (src/tools/toolTestHarness.ts). Do not seed with openAttempt, or seed raw rows, for anything the real path can do.
- vi.stubEnv MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_TASK_ID and MOE_SESSION_ID to '' (seat env leaks; Serena gotcha-seat-env-leaks-into-daemon-tests), and unstub in afterEach.
- Budget: QA caps the task at 400 net LOC under packages/, so keep this file at about 300 lines or fewer, and the shared helpers at about 60.

Helpers:
- boot(): setupMoeFolder (CONTROL), createEpic, createTask PLANNING unassigned, state.load(). Then submitPlanTool with two steps on 'file.ts' (setupMoeFolder creates that file) gives AWAITING_APPROVAL at planRevision 1. Then state.approveTask(TASK, 1) inside runExclusive (the token route) gives WORKING with approvedPlanRevision 1.
- claim(worker): claimNextTaskTool { workerId, statuses: ['WORKING'], taskId, processStartedAt, host }; return the top-level attemptId and generation.
- serve(worker, sessionId): getContextTool { taskId, workerId, sessionId }; return result.servedContext.
- start/step/task: thin wrappers that pass { workerId, attemptId, generation, sessionId }; complete_task also passes verification { command: 'npm test', exitCode: 0 }.
- restartDaemon(): copy the helper from src/tools/reattachAttempt.test.ts: clearEmitter, a new StateManager on the same testDir, load, runExclusive(reconcileRunningAttempts), purgeAllWorkers.
- reattach(): reattachAttemptTool with the claim identity (runnerId = the worker id, which is what a claim records).
- cutover():
  - first expect h.state.updateSettings({ executionProfile: 'verified-local' }) to reject with codeName EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY; the validated path refuses it;
  - then hand-edit project.json settings.executionProfile = 'verified-local', which is all an operator edit can do;
  - then restartDaemon(), so the edit takes effect.

Scenario A (DoD2), one it():
1. boot(); claim W; serve(W, S1). Expect receiptStatus 'recorded', planRevision 1 and approvedPlanRevision 1, and keep the stored receipt R = getAttempt(...).contextReceipt.
2. cutover(). The attempt is now reconciling: a strict start_step is refused ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING. reattach() returns it to running.
3. Call get_context NO more times. start_step and complete_step on step-1 pass the strict gates on R. restartDaemon() again: start_step on step-2 is refused ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING until reattach(). Then start_step and complete_step on step-2 pass on the same R.
4. After every progress write, assert:
   - planRevision === 1 and approvedPlanRevision === 1;
   - the attempt's contextReceipt toEqual R: same id, packetId, servedAt, planRevision and sessionId.
   Execution-only progress, restarts and reattach neither revise approval nor invalidate the receipt. getAttempt(...).stepCompletions maps to [['step-1', 1], ['step-2', 1]].
5. complete_task is refused EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY. The certification gate stays closed: nothing here enables verified-local. The attempt is still running (step 1's hardening) and the task is still WORKING.
6. A contrast, so the test discriminates. A material DoD edit (state.runExclusive(() => state.updateTask(TASK, { definitionOfDone: [...] }))) moves planRevision to 2. complete_task is then refused PLAN_REVISION_NOT_APPROVED, and stays refused after serve(W, S1) records a rev-2 receipt: a receipt never grants approval.

Run this file alone in the snapshot. If a scenario exposes a real defect:
- fix it in the owning production file, with a test, only if that keeps the task within its 5 files and 400 LOC;
- otherwise post the evidence and moe.report_blocked;
- never weaken an assertion to match behaviour.

E2E: reassignment and the legacy-to-strict cutover's no-backfill rules.

Add these cases to executionContract.e2e.test.ts, reusing step 3's helpers. An in-memory cutover is acceptable here, because Scenario A already proves the restart path: assert that updateSettings refuses verified-local, then set h.state.project!.settings.executionProfile = 'verified-local', as startStepAuthorization.test.ts does.

Scenario B: a reassignment keeps the approval and never transfers a receipt.
- boot(); claim A (gen1); serve(A, SA); A's start_step on step-1.
- Reassign the real way: releaseTaskTool { taskId, workerId: A } leaves the row WORKING and unassigned and closes gen1. Then claim B (gen2); serve(B, SB) gives receiptStatus 'recorded' with generation 2.
- Cutover. Assert approvedPlanRevision is still 1 and planRevision 1: a reassignment needs no re-approval.
- Every refusal below happens before any write. Use a small bytes() snapshot of tasks/ and attempts/, as completionAuthorization.test.ts does.
  - A's start_step/complete_step are refused by the ownership guard. Read assertWorkerOwns in util/enforcement.ts for the exact codeName; don't guess it.
  - B presenting A's gen1 attemptId and generation gets ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED.
  - B presenting A's session id gets CONTEXT_RECEIPT_STALE, with context.stale containing 'sessionId'.
- gen1 keeps A's receipt unchanged as history: workerId A, sessionId SA.
- With its own identity, B enters step-2: start_step passes on RB.

Scenario C1: the cutover never backfills approval.
- createTask WORKING, unassigned, planRevision 1, planApprovedAt set, NO approvedPlanRevision, with a 2-step plan. This is a row approved before revision stamps existed.
- load(); claim W; serve(W, S): servedContext.approvedPlanRevision is null.
- Cutover. start_step is refused PLAN_REVISION_NOT_APPROVED before any write, and task.approvedPlanRevision stays undefined: nothing backfills it from planApprovedAt or status.

Scenario C2: legacy-era progress is never strict evidence, and a rollback restores legacy.
- Use boot() for a token-approved row. claim W; serve.
- start_step and complete_step on step-1 under legacy: no stepCompletions are recorded.
- Cutover. start_step and complete_step on step-2 under strict record evidence [['step-2', 1]].
- complete_task is refused EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_INELIGIBLE with context.steps exactly ['step-1']. Step-1's legacy COMPLETED status is kept and never converted into evidence.
- Roll back: delete settings.executionProfile. The same complete_task call now succeeds with status REVIEW and the attempt finalizing, and the strict evidence stays on the attempt as history.

Keep the cases lean. startStepAuthorization.test.ts and completionAuthorization.test.ts already hold the per-tool refusal matrices; don't duplicate them. This is integration test coverage only, with no production edits unless a real defect surfaces (the step 3 rule applies).

E2E, DoD3: the producer's candidate provenance stays distinct from the current QA attempt.

One it(), on the legacy profile: the real REVIEW path cannot run under verified-local.
1. boot(); claim W (gen1); serve(W, SW); start and complete both steps. recordCandidateTool { id: 'cand-producer', taskId, attemptId: gen1, generation: 1, workerId: W, baseRevision and treeSha (7-40 hex), deliveryTarget: 'refs/heads/moe/work' } returns candidate.attemptId === gen1.
2. complete_task returns REVIEW, with gen1 finalizing. finalizeAttemptTool { taskId, workerId: W, runnerId: W, attemptId: gen1, generation: 1, outcome: 'landed', landedRevision: 40 hex } closes gen1. lifecycle.e2e.test.ts's finalizeLanding shows the call.
3. QA: claimNextTaskTool { workerId: Q, statuses: ['REVIEW'], taskId } opens gen2 with workerId Q. serve(Q, SQ) gives servedContext { attemptId: gen2, generation: 2, receiptStatus: 'recorded' }, while the same payload's currentCandidate.attemptId === gen1.
4. Distinctness:
   - the candidate file's bytes are identical before the QA claim and after the claim, the serve, the check run and the approval;
   - listCandidatesForAttempt(state, gen2) is empty;
   - getAttempt(gen1).contextReceipt still names W/SW, and getAttempt(gen2).contextReceipt names Q/SQ.
5. recordCheckRunTool by QA { candidateId, treeSha: the candidate's, command: 'npm test', exitCode: 0, runnerId: Q, source: 'agent-reported', attemptId: gen2, outcome: 'passed', planRevision: 1 }. The stored run's attemptId is gen2, which is not the candidate's attemptId gen1. Per CQ-V02, CheckRun.attemptId may be a reviewer's, while Candidate.attemptId is always the producer's.
6. The superseded producer identity cannot record bytes once QA holds the row: recordCandidateTool with attemptId gen1 is refused ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED, and no new file appears in .moe/candidates.
7. qaApproveTool { taskId, workerId: Q, candidateId: 'cand-producer', summary } moves the row to DONE. The recorded Review (read it via state/reviewStore.ts or .moe/reviews/) names candidateId 'cand-producer' and reviewerId Q.

Do NOT add a new refusal to record_candidate. Fencing QA's own attempt against producer provenance is CQ-V06's DoD (task-6a5d5a13257b48c9940ae3b22347ff7d); this row only proves the CQ-F identities keep the two distinct.

Mutation probes, in a throwaway copy of the snapshot (never committed); record the results in the step note:
(a) setAttemptPhase rebuilds the record without contextReceipt: Scenario A must fail.
(b) completeStep records stepCompletions under legacy too: Scenario C2 must fail.
(c) step 1's early readiness assertion is removed: step 1's test must fail.
(d) recordCandidate.ts's assertAttemptCurrent call is deleted: this scenario must fail.
Run the e2e file and the two step 1/2 files focused.

Document the completion readiness order (the only docs edit this row owns; CQ-F12b did the reference sweep).

In docs/MCP_SERVER.md, `### moe.complete_task`, as CQ-F12b left it, add one or two sentences:
- Readiness (EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY, -32003) is asserted together with the other refusals: after the strict identity, approval, receipt and evidence gates, before the consolidationBranch check, and before the attempt moves to `finalizing`.
- So a refused completion writes nothing, leaves the attempt running, and a retry gets the same refusal.
- On a verified-local row, readiness now precedes BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL.
- The store's progression backstop still runs inside the write.

If steps 1-5 proved any CQ-F12b statement inaccurate, correct it in the same file and say so in the step note. None is expected.

Preserve peer bytes: edit only those lines, and make no other doc edits. Re-run F12b's drift test so it stays green: `npx vitest run src/util/executionContractDocs.test.ts` (in the snapshot).

comments.author: qa-b0c1741e
comments.content:
CQ-F04 (task-076a0bd3) docs hand-forward, recorded by QA at approval (DONE 2026-10-25, completion 3bb12fc). F04 updated only docs/MCP_SERVER.md, in the "Durable authorization (approvedPlanRevision)" block under Plan approval CAS. Per its approved plan, F12 owes:
1. docs/SCHEMA.md: add Task.approvedPlanRevision?: number next to planRevision, plus a short subsection covering:
   - It is daemon-owned. Only approveTask's PLAN_APPROVED write sets it, in the same image as WORKING/planApprovedAt, and only when it equals the revision that write commits.
   - Absent means an unchecked or legacy approval. Null is never written, and a stored null or non-integer reads as absent.
   - Nothing backfills it from status or planApprovedAt.

2. PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md:
   - Token-free approvals record no stamp: an omitted-token APPROVE_TASK or drag, relaxed set_task_status, and SPEED/TURBO (F05).
   - A human approval cancels the SPEED timer only after its write lands.
   - The verified-local omission guard (INVALID_INPUT on expectedPlanRevision) sits behind EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY.
   - Revision-less approval is accepted only until CQ-F04b (task-c619879e) lands.
Consumers (F06-F08) must treat only that safe-integer equality as authorization.

That is either a token-checked human approval (PLAN_APPROVED) or a SPEED/TURBO automatic approval of the revision its plan submission committed (PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED).
   (c) Replace "and SPEED/TURBO auto-approval, which is not fenced yet (CQ-F05)" with the new facts:
   - TURBO stamps approvedPlanRevision = the submitted revision, in the same write as WORKING and planApprovedAt.
   - A SPEED timer approves only the revision it was armed for. After a plan, DoD or contract change it WITHHOLDS: no task write and no activity, plus a #general system message naming both revisions. The row then waits for a human token approval or a resubmission, and no timer is re-armed for the newer revision.
   - The restart re-arm binds to executionPolicySnapshot.planRevision, captured in the PLAN_SUBMITTED write.
   - A legacy row with no snapshot binds to its current revision, which is today's behaviour.
   - When the snapshot or revision can't be read, the re-arm records the existing 'SPEED mode auto-approval failed' activity and leaves the row unarmed. The re-arm never throws at daemon start.
2. docs/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md, "Limits" list: two bullets are superseded:
   - "SPEED / TURBO automatic approval policy is unchanged and token-free by design";
   - "A SPEED callback already queued behind the state mutex can still fire after a human refusal". After F05, a queued callback can approve only the revision it was armed for, and the store re-checks it in the approval write.
3. docs/SCHEMA.md approvedPlanRevision subsection (already owed from F04, comment-8e824b16): name the PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED writes as stampers too.

comments.author: worker-07cd2c56
comments.content:
CQ-F05 (task-c7d520ba) worker follow-up to the architect's docs hand-forward. There is no design deviation, but two details need precise wording in the F12 docs:
1. "Withheld: no task write and no activity" means no TASK activity. The #general system message itself logs the usual non-task MESSAGE_CREATED activity, as every chat post does.
2. A withheld row stays AWAITING_APPROVAL with no live timer. Every daemon restart therefore re-arms it, still bound to the snapshot's (older) revision, and withholds again with one more #general notice. It never approves the newer revision. The notice text names both revisions and says "Approve the current revision from the board, or reject the plan and resubmit it."
Implementation: submitPlan.ts armSpeedModeApproval(…, revision) and rearmSpeedModeApprovals; taskStore.updateTask accepts the stamp on PLAN_APPROVED || PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED.

comments.author: architect-6e3edf85
comments.content:
F06 docs hand-forward. F06 rev 1 deliberately leaves docs to F12; re-verify against F06's landed code first.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md, moe.get_context section:
- New `sessionId` input. It is the receiving session's incarnation exactly as the runner names it: the wrapper's MOE_SESSION_ID `<workerId>@<preflight-iso>`. There is no env fallback. A malformed value is refused for every view, and null counts as malformed.
- New `servedContext` block on default and view:"full" reads: {taskId, planRevision, approvedPlanRevision, attemptId, generation, receiptStatus, receiptId, packetId}.
- receiptStatus values: identity-unreadable, no-session, no-running-attempt, not-attempt-owner, recorded, record-failed.
- packetId = sha256 of the response minus servedContext.
- view:"status" never records a receipt.
- A receipt records what was served; it is never approval.

docs/SCHEMA.md:
- ExecutionAttempt.contextReceipt (ServedContextReceipt): one latest-wins slot, written only for a running attempt by its own worker.
- approvedPlanRevision is absent, never null.

On the F12 DoD item "execution-only progress does not invalidate receipts by revising approval": a receipt records the planRevision it was served at. Only material plan, DoD or contract changes advance that revision.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) One task carrying every hand-forward: rejected. It needs about 12 files across proxy, daemon, scripts and docs, over submit_plan's hard limit of 10 and QA's 400 net LOC cap. Split instead: CQ-F12a (task-b5f743bc) takes the proxy completion stamping and the transport docs, CQ-F12b (task-3ead73b3) the reference docs and a drift test, and this row stays the single epic-final integration and hardening task. (2) Seeding strict rows with openAttempt, as the F07/F08 tests do: rejected for the e2e, because it would duplicate their refusal matrices and bypass the real claim, restart, release and QA paths. Claim admission refuses verified-local, so strictness is engaged the way an operator would: a legacy claim, then a hand-edited cutover (the 'legacy-to-strict cutover' in the objective). (3) Adding a record_candidate refusal for a reviewer's attempt: rejected; CQ-V06's DoD ('QA own attempt is fenced without confusing candidate producer provenance') owns it. F12 proves the distinctness that CQ-F's identities preserve. (4) Exporting taskStore's private assertProgressionReady for the hardening: rejected. Calling assertExecutionProfileReady(resolveTaskExecutionProfile(...)) directly is the claimEligibility idiom, and it evaluates the identical expression for complete_task's WORKING->REVIEW write.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Verified at HEAD 66ef204:
- validators.ts refuses executionProfile 'verified-local' on every validated settings update (assertExecutionProfileReady), so a cutover can only come from a hand-edited project.json.
- Only claim_next_task and wait_for_task apply execution admission (util/claimEligibility.ts executionAdmissionRefusal). reattach_attempt, get_context, start_step, complete_step and complete_task do not.
- assertExecutionAuthorized (util/executionAuthorization.ts) is strict when the task's resolved profile OR the open attempt's snapshot is verified-local. Its order: identity shape/fence, strictness, missing identity (STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED), running own attempt (ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING), approval (approvedPlanRevision === planRevision, PLAN_REVISION_NOT_APPROVED), receipt (CONTEXT_RECEIPT_STALE). The tools run assertWorkerHoldsTask/assertWorkerOwns and assertContextFetched BEFORE it.
- Receipts live in ExecutionAttempt.contextReceipt: one latest-wins slot, recorded only for the running attempt's own worker who is also the assignee. setAttemptPhase spreads the record, so reconcile and reattach keep it.
- stepCompletions are recorded only under strict, by recordStepCompletion, before the task write.
- completeTask.ts moves the attempt to finalizing BEFORE updateTask's progression backstop, which is the F08 hardening candidate.
- The current candidate is the latest by createdAt (reviewStore.resolveReviewedCandidate / getContext). Candidate.attemptId is the producer; CheckRun.attemptId may be a reviewer's (CQ-V02). A REVIEW claim opens a new generation once finalize_attempt has closed the producer's attempt.
- Patterns to reuse: the restartDaemon helper in tools/reattachAttempt.test.ts; the full real-tool flow including finalizeLanding in __e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts; the refused()/bytes() helpers in tools/completionAuthorization.test.ts.
- submit_plan exempts newFiles declared anywhere in the plan from the existence gate, so steps 4-5 can cite the e2e file.
planningNotes.risks:
- QA's 400 net LOC cap over packages/: budget about 300 for the e2e, 45 for the store tests and 15 for the rest.
- The two held-out race files must stay byte-identical. A diff touching them is a QA reject.
- The shared checkout's node_modules is a Windows install: run vitest only in the isolated Linux snapshot, and never run proxy npm test in the shared checkout (it deletes the shared dist).
- Seat env (MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_SESSION_ID) leaks into daemon tests; stub it, and run gates with env -i.
- Refusal precedence: a non-assignee is refused by ownership before the attempt fence, so assert the real codeName.
- finalize_attempt 'landed' needs a 40-hex landedRevision.
- Keep a single candidate before the QA claim, so createdAt ordering cannot flake.
- restartDaemon must clearEmitter.
- The hardening makes NOT_READY precede BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL on a verified-local row; that is documented in step 6.
- Docs written by F12b may need a one-line correction if this row's tests disprove something.
- Never enable verified-local or weaken assertExecutionProfileReady: the cutover is a hand edit that the gate still refuses at completion.
